P:Why retrieve in both directions?
M:The shared space should support both text to numeric and numeric to text retrieval.
Q:TEXT <-> NUMERIC
V:validated
A:Both directions test the common representation.

P:What does a positive alignment margin indicate?
M:The correct pair scores higher than the strongest incorrect candidate.
Q:POSITIVE > HARD NEGATIVE
V:validated
A:The correct pair is separated from its strongest competitor.

P:Why does cross-modal retrieval matter for memory?
M:One memory can contain several representations that must remain connected.
Q:MEMORY TEXT <-> MEMORY SIGNAL
V:validated
A:It keeps representations of the same memory linked.

P:How should alignment be validated?
M:Use exact retrieval, class retrieval, margin validation and deterministic repeated inference.
Q:INSTANCE + CLASS + MARGIN + CONSISTENCY
V:validated
A:Validate identity, semantics, separation and consistency.

P:Why test exact instance retrieval?
M:Two records can share a semantic class while representing different events.
Q:CLASS MATCH != INSTANCE MATCH
V:validated
A:Exact retrieval verifies the correct paired instance.

P:Why is cross-modal retrieval useful in engineering?
M:A maintenance description can retrieve its corresponding machine measurements.
Q:MAINTENANCE TEXT -> MEASUREMENTS
V:validated
A:It connects engineering language with measured evidence.
